subject: Urgent: transient inference latency impacting batch pipelines
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@northbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: transient inference latency impacting batch pipelines

Samira —

I wanted to let you know we’ve detected a transient increase in tail latency for batch scoring jobs that may have affected several of your overnight runs between 02:40–03:10 UTC this morning. We’ve opened a priority incident and are on a live bridge with engineering now.

Immediate notes: 
- Symptoms: intermittent 5xxs and request timeouts when sequences exceed 3k tokens; elevated p95/p99.
- Impact: some batch jobs retried and queued; a small subset of predictions returned with delayed completion (seconds to tens of seconds).
- Customer-facing action: we are prioritizing queued jobs and will provide a timeline for any re-runs or credits if needed.

I’ll keep this short — Ben is on the bridge and will post an interim status in the next 15 minutes. We’ll share a concise incident note and an executive summary for your leaders as soon as we have stabilization.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge_notes_20270918.pdf (summary of current bridge roles / message log)

From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@northbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@northbridge.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: transient inference latency impacting batch pipelines

Thanks Jordan —

We noticed a few failed batches this morning in our reconciliation pipeline and a spike in latency alerts. Appreciate the quick flag. Can you confirm whether customer data was affected or whether this was an internal resource scheduling issue? We’re prepping an internal note for our ops team and need any immediate mitigations.

— Samira
Director, Data Engineering
Northbridge Financial

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@northbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: transient inference latency impacting batch pipelines

Samira — quick answers while we triage on the bridge:
- No evidence of data corruption or unauthorized access; requests either timed out or were retried.
- Preliminary root cause looks like a scheduling pressure combined with a model KV-cache fragmentation on a small subset of hosts; more details to follow from infra.
- Immediate mitigation: we’ve temporarily routed your batch traffic to a warm pool in a different AZ and drained the affected hosts; that should clear queued jobs in the next 10–20 minutes.

We’ll confirm once the queue is clear. Sorry for the disruption — we know morning batch windows are sensitive.

— Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@northbridge.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Bridge update: stabilization in progress (details + next steps)

On behalf of the bridge — current operational status: 

1) What we saw: between 02:40–03:08 UTC an elevated thread of long-tail token sequences caused uneven KV-cache pressure on four inference nodes, causing GC-like stalls and connection timeouts for in-flight requests.

2) Immediate remediation performed: 
- Traffic for affected customer pool (northbridge-prod-batch) diverted to a warm reserve; affected hosts drained.
- Rolling restarts of the 4 hosts with updated kernel tunables applied.
- We bumped request-level timeouts and enabled aggressive backoff for client retries to avoid retry storms.

3) Impact estimate: 
- ~3% of batch jobs experienced delayed completion and retried; ~0.4% returned 5xx and will need re-run.
- No data exfiltration or integrity issues identified.

4) Next artifacts we’ll deliver in 2 hours: 
- A short timeline CSV (timeline_draft.csv) with timestamps and affected request ids.
- Network trace and kernel logs (network-trace.txt) for your SREs.
- A one-page executive note for your leadership.

5) Owner & escalation: Ben (infra), Karthik (runtime), Jordan (customer comms).

We’ll update again at 10:15 PT or sooner if there’s a material change.

— Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: network-trace.txt (truncated)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@northbridge.com>, Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@northbridge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Executive summary: morning latency incident — status and remediation plan

Hi Samira / Ethan —

I’m Stephanie (Head of Customer Success Operations) — wanted to provide a concise executive summary and the immediate steps we are taking.

Summary: A transient scheduling and KV-cache fragmentation event on a small subset of hosts caused elevated p99 latency and some batch job failures between 02:40–03:10 UTC. By 03:30 UTC traffic had been routed off the affected hosts and the majority of backlog cleared.

Customer impact: We estimate ~0.4% of total prediction calls returned 5xx and ~3% of batch jobs saw delays that triggered retries. We have not observed incorrect outputs.

Remediation and commitments: 
- Short term: re-run support — Redwood will provide a prioritized re-run of any failed batch jobs at no incremental cost if required.
- Medium term (2 weeks): runtime patch to reduce KV-cache fragmentation and updated scheduling threshold to prevent the same interaction.
- Long term (60 days): a quantization of capacity planning across batch pools and a change to the autoscaler to account for long-sequence workloads.

We will share a formal postmortem with timelines and action owners within 72 hours. In the meantime, Ben’s team has uploaded the bridge notes and the timeline CSV to the shared Drive link.

Please let me know if your leadership would like a short 15-minute sync this afternoon — I’m available 2:00–4:00 PT.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge_notes_20270918.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@northbridge.com>, Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@northbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & next steps — post-incident actions and timeline

Samira / Ethan —

Thanks again for your patience this morning. Quick summary of agreed next steps and owners: 

1) Re-run support: If you identify specific job ids that failed, send them to me and we will prioritize re-runs this week (Owner: Jordan / CS ops).
2) Postmortem: Draft to be shared in 48–72 hours with a technical appendix (Owner: Karthik / Runtime).
3) Patch rollout: Runtime patch and scheduler tuning planned for the next 14 business days; we’ll provide a staged rollout schedule (Owner: Ben).
4) Credits: If re-runs materially impacted your SLAs, we’ll apply a pro-rated credit — we’ll confirm after the postmortem (Owner: Stephanie).

Links: incident log (HS-23145), timeline CSV, bridge notes are in the Drive link we shared earlier.

If helpful I can also coordinate the 15-minute leadership sync Stephanie offered — propose 2:30 PT today; please let me know.

— Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
